statement: The Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park's public Aṉangu cultural guidance describes Tjukurpa as ongoing law, spirituality and responsibility toward land and kin; it explicitly distinguishes openly shareable stories from restricted knowledge and says stories are transmitted to the appropriate people.

sources.citation: Parks Australia / Uluṟu–Kata Tjuṯa National Park, 'Tjukurpa', sections 'Tjukurpa law and spirituality' and 'Kinship and passing down of Tjukurpa', https://uluru.gov.au/discover/culture/tjukurpa/
sources.author: Aṉangu traditional owner knowledge via Parks Australia
sources.access_note: Full public park cultural page read including stated non-disclosure of secret/sacred material. Only publicly approved general teaching summarized.

does_not_demonstrate: Ancient regional occupation dates do not establish the age of any specific Tjukurpa account.
Public descriptions do not authorize disclosure of restricted or initiatory content.
Tjukurpa is a living system of responsibilities; a Western category like 'myth' alone is insufficient.
adversarial_counter: Even official public educational wording is a limited framing of a living Aṉangu knowledge system; further content needs community authorization.
notes: Institutional-source audit. Scope: named public page and its content only; no tradition founding-year inference. Independent historical / community review required before status change.
